verdict: Medtronic's sales jumped 14% to $9.8B — unusually fast for the medical-device giant — as heart treatments surged, and profit rose 41% to $1.5B.

segments.name: Cardiovascular
segments.note: Heart devices — pacemakers, heart valves and ablation catheters. Electrophysiology (treating irregular heartbeats) grew in the high 20s.

segments.name: Neuroscience
segments.note: Brain and spine devices, including spinal surgery systems and brain stimulators.

segments.name: Medical Surgical
segments.note: Surgical tools and patient-monitoring equipment used in operating rooms and hospitals.

segments.name: Diabetes
segments.note: Insulin pumps and glucose sensors. Medtronic is in the process of separating this business into its own company.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Small remaining items Medtronic groups as 'Other'.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: The global sales force that works with hospitals and surgeons, plus the back office.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing the next generation of devices and running clinical trials.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Accounting write-down of technology bought in past acquisitions — non-cash, and excluded from non-GAAP results.

otherDetail: Other non-operating income of $190M — including gains on minority investments — less $186M of net interest expense.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Heart treatments led the surge
takeaways.text: Cardiovascular sales rose 20% to $3.9B, with electrophysiology — catheter treatments for irregular heartbeats — growing in the high 20s on pulsed-field ablation demand.

takeaways.title: Growth was broad, not one product
takeaways.text: All four portfolios grew at double-digit rates: Cardiovascular +20%, Diabetes +17%, Neuroscience +10% and Medical Surgical +10%.

takeaways.title: The non-GAAP gap is mostly amortization
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $1.45 versus $1.14 GAAP. The biggest difference is $412M of amortization of acquired technology — a real accounting cost, but not cash out the door this quarter.

footerNote: Medtronic notes this schedule is intentionally rounded to the nearest million; the reported pre-tax line is $1M higher than the rounded lines sum to, and that rounding is absorbed in the net other-income line here. This is Medtronic's fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026); its fiscal Q2 ends in late October and had not been reported yet. Net income of $1,470M is attributable to Medtronic; consolidated net income was $1,479M.
